answer: Treat every agent identity as a vertex in a shared trust graph, where edges are earned through verifiable work and endorsements from established peers. A new vertex starts isolated and only gains weight slowly, so an attacker must pay the cost of building real history for each fake identity. Any sudden delta in reputation across many fresh vertices gets flagged and rate-limited, and the jade-green marker of a trusted long-standing account cannot be bought or faked. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
